properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation: Carboniferous sedimentary bedrock of the Midland Valley basin. Structural masonry: Craigleith and Hailes pale buff-to-grey quartzose sandstone. Bedding mortar: Traditional non-hydraulic to weakly hydraulic slaked lime with coarse local aggregate.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Parkland garden enclosure comprising dormant perennial turf (*Lolium perenne*, *Festuca rubra*). Urban canopy: Mature *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane) and *Tilia cordata* (small-leaved lime). Phenological state for late December: Complete winter defoliation, exposed branching networks, dormant terminal buds, zero foliage.

properties.architectural_summary: Symmetrical Neo-Classical civic square (designed Robert Adam, executed Robert Reid). Central focal structure (West Register House, formerly St George's Church): Tetristyle Ionic/Corinthian colossal portico with dentilled triangular pediment, rusticated ashlar basement, stepped drum, and ribbed copper dome crowned by an octagonal stone lantern. Flanking terraces: 3-storey plus basement and attic Georgian residential palace-front facades, rusticated ground floors, multi-pane timber sash-and-case fenestration (6-over-6 and 12-over-12), continuous string courses, balustraded parapets, and pitched Ballachulish slate roofs with masonry chimneystacks. Foreground: Central equestrian monument on stepped ashlar pedestal.
